A lump of charcoal that is a book. In 79 CE Vesuvius buried a Roman villa at Herculaneum and baked its library into rolls of carbon that crumble at a touch: the only library of the Greek and Roman world to survive. For more than 270 years, people have tried to read it.

We follow the black lumps from the tunnels of the 1750s to Piaggio's unrolling machine and the Epicurean philosopher Philodemus; X-ray scans, the En-Gedi scroll and the problem of black ink on a black page; the Vesuvius Challenge, from the first word, 'purple', to the grand prize and the first titles; and the first scroll read end to end, announced in June 2026. Verdict: Established that sealed rolls can be read. A whole scroll read: Strong evidence, awaiting outside review. More books in the unexcavated villa: Plausible.

long.hook: A computer, two thousand years old?
long.caption:
A lump of corroded bronze from a shipwreck off the Greek island of Antikythera turned out to hold thirty gear wheels and thousands of tiny Greek letters: a calculator of the sky, made more than two thousand years ago. How did it work, who made it, and is it really out of its time?

Verdict: Established. Weigh it yourself: residualcontinuum.com
long.description:
A lump of corroded bronze from a shipwreck off the Greek island of Antikythera turned out to hold thirty gear wheels and thousands of tiny Greek letters: a calculator of the sky, made more than two thousand years ago. How did it work, who made it, and is it really out of its time?

We follow it from the sponge divers of 1900 and the gear noticed in 1902, through Derek de Solla Price's radiographs and Michael Wright's tomography, to the X-ray scans of 2005 and the 2021 model of its lost planets; we sort what is read in the bronze from what is inferred, weigh its dates, and test the out-of-place claim. Verdict: Established, a Greek geared calculator of the Sun, the Moon, eclipses, calendars and games. Its planetary display: Strong evidence. The 2021 gear-by-gear model: Plausible. Its maker and place: Open question. An origin out of its time: Ruled out.
